introduction: Illinois Legal Aid Online offers legal information, forms and a tool to find legal help. Use the issue and ZIP-code search to locate relevant resources.
description: Illinois Legal Aid Online offers legal information, forms and a tool to find legal help. Use the issue and ZIP-code search to locate relevant resources.

sections.who: You can browse information and forms. For a lawyer referral, the tool asks about the issue, location, household and income; individual legal organizations decide whether they can accept your case.
sections.get: The site covers housing, benefits, family and other legal topics. Its Get Legal Help tool can point to a lawyer, forms or information, and its self-help-center list can be filtered by county.
sections.docs:
• Your ZIP code or the location of the legal problem.
  • The type of issue and any court deadline.
  • Household and gross income information for the matching tool.
  • Relevant notices or court papers for a later provider intake.
sections.apply:
1. Open Get Legal Help

    Use the matching tool.

  2. Choose the help needed

    Select a lawyer, forms or information and answer the relevant questions.

  3. Contact the listed provider

    Check intake and case acceptance; submitting the tool does not appoint a lawyer.
sections.after: Keep responding to court notices while seeking help. Ask the provider to clarify whether it has agreed to represent you.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using ILAO topics and form library, legal help matching and center directory. The administering organization decides eligibility.

faqs: Does the form mean my case is accepted?
No. The tool explicitly says completing it does not mean an organization has taken the case.
Can I look for forms without requesting a lawyer?
Yes. Forms and legal information are separate selections in the tool.
Your ZIP code or the ZIP code of the legal problem.
Can I find a local self-help center?
Yes. The tool includes a county-filtered center directory.
